page: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a memory-optimized and storage-focused virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI.

The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, it bundles a substantial 2880 GB NVMe SSD and is designated as Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3078.28 and Geekbench single-core reaching 2071.0, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6154.66 and Geekbench multi-core score of 4736.0. However, memory read bandwidth is weak, measuring 303.46 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 36.73 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though write bandwidth remains average at 27.93 GB/sec. Database operations and static web serving throughput also fall into the lower performance tiers.

Given the combination of high-capacity local NVMe SSD storage and a generous memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server is well-suited for storage-heavy workloads, local database caching, and memory-intensive applications that do not require massive parallel processing. The primary tradeoff lies in its moderate multi-core scaling and weaker memory read bandwidth, making it less optimal for high-throughput web serving or large-scale software compilation.

Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 instance includes a massive 2880 GB local NVMe SSD and is Premium Storage capable. Performance benchmarks highlight strong single-core capabilities, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2071.0, alongside average multi-core performance.
